# 与客户沟通，打造 SEO 与 AI 优化工具

- 作者：Flavio Amiel（@fba）
- 原帖发布时间：2026-08-14 04:39（北京时间）
- 原帖：https://x.com/fba/status/2088002406999064681
- 收藏日期：2026-10-29

## 中文全文

这样的故事让我兴奋。

我正在照着同样的方法做。

我的工具面向中小企业，具体来说是 SEO 代理机构和网站组合构建者。

它做的是其他工具似乎也在做、但实际上没有真正做到的事情：通过智能体审查并修复你的网站，让你更有机会在 AI 和 SEO 中获得排名。

而我花时间最多的地方是什么？和客户交谈。我认为，没有比这更好的方式来打造出色体验，并找到产品与市场的契合点（PMF）。

### 原帖中的引用预览（非被引用文章全文）

[Nick Velkovski @nikolak47](<https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2087955579151217022>)

我们在 3 年多一点的时间里，完全靠自力更生，把 @heyreach_io 从只有一个每月付费 $139 的客户，做到了 $17M ARR（年度经常性收入）。

我的一位朋友说，如果我今天失去这一切，一年之内，我仍然能再做出一家至少达到 $1M ARR 的公司。他说得对。以下就是我会采取的具体做法：

1. 我不会试图做太多创新。

我会再次自力更生地创办一家向中小企业销售的 B2B SaaS 公司。和上次一样。

创造一个品类很贵，无论金钱还是时间成本都很高。所以，我会找到一个已经存在的品类，从中选一个具体功能，把它做到好 10 倍，然后打包成一个非常难以拒绝的方案。

市场已经存在，你就不用花好几年去说服别人，这个问题确实存在。而且，如果你真心相信自己能把某件事做到好 10 倍，通常意味着你已经足够深入地研究了这个问题，有了自己的切入角度。这样的方案本身也会承担很多销售工作。我会用 Pylon 或 Atlas 作为这里的例子。

我们推出 @heyreach_io 时，那个市场已经有 400+ 款工具。

2. 我会在觉得自己准备好之前，就早早进入市场。

只要有了一个能运转的东西，我就会开始卖。先从自己的人脉入手，尽可能获取各种社会认同，再把它展示给尽可能多的人。

如果今天从头开始，我会在测试版之后立刻上 AppSumo。那些用户大多不会是理想客户画像（ICP），其中很多人也不会留下来……但他们会告诉你产品所有不对劲的地方，而且能带来大量维持经营的资金。把它当作一轮种子前融资。

3. 我会从零学习如何销售自己的产品。

一个人有 20+ 年销售经验也无所谓。销售你的产品是一件独立的事，每个人都要从起点开始。

我会专注于学会客户的表达方式，再用他们的语言与他们交流。最初推出多个 LinkedIn 发送账号功能时，我们把它叫作“多账号外联”。后来，是客户彻底改变了它的名字。

4. 我会先实现盈利，然后全力追求 PMF。

@VukConfidential 开始为我们提供咨询时，告诉过我一件事：一旦实现盈利，你就能喘口气了。

因此，我会一心实现盈利，然后才全力以赴寻找产品与市场的契合点（PMF）。

在这个阶段，你能犯的最大错误，就是关注流程、规则、优化、使命或愿景。这个阶段的你不是 CEO，而是一个试图判断产品是否有人需要的产品人。

没有 PMF 时，无论你做什么，都不起作用。一旦找到 PMF，无论你做什么，在一定程度上都能起作用。

找到 PMF，是公司命运的关键时刻；在找到它之前，你都在走向死亡。

---

## 英文原文

Stories like this get me excited.

I’m literally applying this same playbook.

My tool is done for SMBs, namely SEO agencies and portfolio builders.

It does what other tools kind of do but not really: audits and fixes your website  with agents, so that you have higher chances of ranking in AI and SEO.

And where I’m spending the most time? Talking with my customers. I don’t think there is a better way to create an outstanding experience and hit PMF

### Quoted preview

[Nick Velkovski @nikolak47](<https://x.com/nikolak47/status/2087955579151217022>)

We took @heyreach_io from one customer paying $139/mo to $17M ARR in a little over 3 years, fully bootstrapped.

One of my friends told me that if I lost all of it today, in a year I'd have a business doing at least $1M ARR again. He's right, and here's exactly how I'd do it:

1. I wouldn't try to innovate much

I'd bootstrap a B2B SaaS selling to SMBs again. Same thing as last time.

Creating a category is expensive, both in money and in time. So I'd find a category that already exists, pick one specific function inside it, and make that function 10x better. Then put it in an offer that's really hard to say no to.

The market is already there, so you're not spending years convincing anyone the problem exists. And if you honestly believe you can be 10x better at something, it usually means you've dug into that problem enough to already have an angle. The offer ends up doing a lot of the selling too. Pylon or Atlas are what I'd point at here.

We launched @heyreach_io into a market that already had 400+ tools in it.

2. I'd go to market way before I felt ready

The moment I had something working I'd start selling it. I'd go at my own network first and try to get any social proof I could, then just get the thing in front of as many people as possible.

If I was starting today I'd go on AppSumo right after the beta. Most of those users won't be the ICP and a lot of them won't stick around... but they tell you everything that's wrong with the product, and it generates a lot of runway. Think of it as a pre-seed round.

3. I'd learn how to sell my own product from zero

Doesn't matter if someone has 20+ years in sales. Selling YOUR product is its own thing and everyone starts at the beginning with it.

The part I'd focus on is picking up the lingo of your customers and saying it back to them. When we first launched the feature of multiple LinkedIn senders, we called it "multi-account outreach". It was the customers that completely changed its name.

4. I'd get profitable, then obsess over PMF

@VukConfidential told me something when he started consulting us: you can breathe more easily once you become profitable.

So I'd obsess over becoming profitable, and only after that go all in on reaching PMF.

The biggest mistake you can make at this stage is focusing on processes, rules, optimizations, missions or vision. At this stage you are not a CEO, you are a product person trying to see if there's a need for the product.

When you don't have PMF, whatever you do just doesn't work. Once you get to PMF, whatever you do just works, to some extent.

PMF is the defining moment of your company, and until you reach it you are dying.
